title: DATE (All-Day) vs DATE-TIME Value Type Consistency and Transitions Across Master, UNTIL, EXDATE, and RECURRENCE-ID

citations.verbatim_quote: Value Type:  The default value type is DATE-TIME.  The value type can be set to a DATE value type.  This property MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property contained within the recurring component.  Furthermore, this property MUST be specified as a date with local time if and only if the "DTSTART" property contained within the recurring component is specified as a date with local time.
If the value of the "DTSTART" property is a DATE type value, then the value MUST be the calendar date for the recurrence instance.

The value of the UNTIL rule part MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property.  Furthermore, if the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with local time, then the UNTIL rule part MUST also be specified as a date with local time.  If the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with UTC time or a date with local time and time zone reference, then the UNTIL rule part MUST be specified as a date with UTC time.

Within the "VEVENT" calendar component, this property defines the date and time by which the event ends.  The value type of this property MUST be the same as the "DTSTART" property, and its value MUST be later in time than the value of the "DTSTART" property.

In the iCalendar component, the value data types of the DTSTART, DUE and RECURRENCE-ID properties all MUST be of the same form, either DATE, or DATE WITH LOCAL TIME, or DATE WITH UTC TIME (see Section 3.3.5 of [RFC5545]).  It MUST be DATE if the "showWithoutTime" property value is "true", the "timeZone" property value is null, and the time component is zero in the values of the "start", due", "duration", "estimatedDuration", "recurrenceId" properties, and the "until" property of the RecurrenceRule object, and in any key of the "recurrenceOverrides" property value.

rationale: RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 mandates that RECURRENCE-ID MUST have the same value type (DATE vs DATE-TIME, and floating local time vs UTC/timezone-qualified time) as the DTSTART property of the recurring component; if DTSTART is a DATE value, RECURRENCE-ID MUST be the calendar DATE for the recurrence instance (e.g., YYYYMMDD). Similarly, RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10 requires the RRULE UNTIL part to have the exact same value type as DTSTART (and forbids BYSECOND, BYMINUTE, BYHOUR when DTSTART is a DATE), Section 3.8.2.2 requires DTEND to have the same value type as DTSTART, and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Section 3.2 requires DTSTART, DUE, RECURRENCE-ID, UNTIL, and recurrenceOverrides keys to share a uniform temporal value type. Consequently, all recurrence properties of a series must agree on DATE vs DATE-TIME, and if a whole-series edit transitions the master component's DTSTART between DATE (all-day) and DATE-TIME, any prior DATE or DATE-TIME EXDATEs and RECURRENCE-ID overrides that no longer match the updated value type and recurrence set cannot remain attached in an inconsistent value type.
store_implication:
1. Within any recurring series, the master component's DTSTART value type (DATE vs DATE-TIME) governs the required value type of DTEND/DUE, RRULE UNTIL, EXDATE, RDATE, and the RECURRENCE-ID of all single-instance or split components for that series.
2. For an all-day series (`DTSTART;VALUE=DATE`), single-instance edits/deletions and THIS_AND_FUTURE splits MUST emit `RECURRENCE-ID;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, `EXDATE;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, and `UNTIL=YYYYMMDD` (date-only, never midnight `YYYYMMDDT000000Z`).
3. When a whole-series edit (`recurrence_id=None`) transitions a recurring series between `DATE` (all-day) and `DATE-TIME` (timed), the updated component's DTSTART and DTEND/DUE must both use the new value type, and any prior EXDATE values or RECURRENCE-ID overrides of the old value type that do not match occurrences of the updated master component MUST be pruned.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: All-day recurring event (`DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20250501`, `RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3`): editing the 2025-05-02 instance with Range=NONE MUST set `RECURRENCE-ID;VALUE=DATE:20250502` (not `RECURRENCE-ID:20250502T000000`).

All-day recurring event split or deleted with THIS_AND_FUTURE at `20250503`: the truncated master's RRULE MUST set `UNTIL=20250502` (a DATE value, one calendar day before `2025-05-03`), never `UNTIL=20250502T235959` (which violates RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10).

Transitioning a recurring series from all-day (`DATE: 2025-05-01`) to timed (`DATE-TIME: 2025-05-01T09:00:00`) via a whole-series edit (`recurrence_id=None`): prior `VALUE=DATE` EXDATEs (e.g. `2025-05-02`) and `VALUE=DATE` override components (`RECURRENCE-ID;VALUE=DATE:20250502`) no longer match the timed `DATE-TIME` recurrence set and must be pruned so the resulting calendar does not violate RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4's value-type equality requirement.

scenarios.name: all_day_single_instance_edit_and_delete_preserve_date_value_type
scenarios.description: On an all-day (VALUE=DATE) daily series, deleting May 2 (Range=NONE) records a DATE EXDATE (2025-05-02) and editing May 3 (Range=NONE) creates a RECURRENCE-ID override with a DATE recurrence_id (20250503) and DATE dtstart/dtend.

scenarios.name: whole_series_transition_from_date_to_datetime_prunes_date_exdate_and_override
scenarios.description: Converting an all-day recurring series (with a DATE EXDATE and a DATE RECURRENCE-ID override) to a timed DATE-TIME series via a whole-series edit updates DTSTART/DTEND to DATE-TIME and prunes the incompatible DATE EXDATE and DATE override.

audit_notes: Verified +/- 40 lines around all five citations in rfc5545.txt (Sections 3.8.4.4, 3.3.10, 3.8.2.2) and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar.txt (Section 3.2).

Reclassified authority from RFC_5545 to STORE_POLICY during Wave 3 adversarial audit: while RFC 5545 Sections 3.8.4.4, 3.3.10, and 3.8.2.2 strictly mandate uniform value types (DATE vs DATE-TIME) across DTSTART, DTEND, UNTIL, and RECURRENCE-ID, the store behavior of automatically pruning incompatible prior EXDATEs and RECURRENCE-ID overrides when a whole-series edit transitions DTSTART between DATE and DATE-TIME is an active store maintenance policy grounded in those RFC invariants.
Confirmed 100% clean-room independence and mathematical consistency across both scenarios.
